original_question: In higher-dimensional single-input time-optimal control systems q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, there are examples of extremals with accumulating switching points whose qualitative structure survives small perturbations of the system. Are such extremals actually time-optimal?
target_in_paper: Section I.A (“Singularities of time-optimal trajectories”), in the paragraph titled “Higher dimensions”: the unnumbered open problem asking whether the known examples of extremals with accumulating switching points whose structure survives C∞-small perturbations are actually optimal.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core target very well: it identifies the correct control system class qdot = f(q) + u g(q) with |u| <= 1, the higher-dimensional setting, the phenomenon of accumulating switching points, the persistence of that chattering structure under small perturbations, and the exact issue raised in the paper—whether those known extremals are truly time-optimal.
missing_details: The paper is in the smooth category here: f and g are assumed to be C∞ vector fields on an n-dimensional manifold M.
The problem is a fixed-endpoint time-optimal problem for the system qdot = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, q in M.
Admissible controls are measurable functions, and admissible trajectories are Lipschitz curves in M.
The relevant discussion is subsection I.A, where (f,g) is treated as a generic pair of vector fields; your draft does not mention this local scope.
The perturbations are specifically C∞-small perturbations of the system/pair (f,g), not just unspecified small perturbations.
The paper does not specify a sharp dimensional threshold; it says only that this phenomenon is expected 'starting from some (not very big) dimension' and speaks loosely of 'higher dimensions'.
The sentence in the paper is about the known examples cited in references [21] and [37], not a blanket claim about every extremal with accumulating switching points.

To be fully paper-faithful, the question should ask whether these extremals are time-optimal trajectories, not broaden to whether such behavior is generically optimal or whether all perturbation-stable chattering extremals are optimal.
The neighboring question in subsection I.B is different: in the real-analytic setting, whether one can always choose a time-optimal trajectory with at most countably many switching points.
refined_question: For the fixed-endpoint time-optimal problem for a smooth single-input control-affine system on an n-dimensional manifold M, qdot = f(q) + u g(q) with |u| <= 1, where f and g are C∞ vector fields, are the known higher-dimensional extremals with accumulating switching points whose chattering structure survives C∞-small perturbations of the pair (f,g) actually time-optimal trajectories?
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s actual intent. The nearest official formulation is not a numbered conjecture but the unnumbered question in Section I.A, page 2, under “Higher dimensions.” After setting up the smooth single-input time-optimal problem on page 1 and discussing generic regularity/switching behavior, Agrachev writes that there are examples of extremals with accumulating switching points whose structure survives small perturbations, but that nobody knows whether these extremals are optimal. That is the precise narrow target. It is more faithful than shifting to the neighboring generic n = 3 question about finiteness of switchings, and also more faithful than the distinct real-analytic question in Section I.B about replacing a given optimal trajectory by one with at most countably many switching points.
